To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SSC magnet test stands are ready for the first magnet to be tested in 1992.

the SSC magnet test stands have been successfully operated at superfluid temperatures and are capable of providing the refrigeration necessary to cool the magnet to 1.8K and maintain the temperature at that level.
a full length, full scale, superconducting SSC main ring dipole magnet has been operated successfully in the superfluid regime.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and operation of cryogenic test stands capable of operating at 2.0-4.5 K and 1.8-4.5K, respectively.
the development of a cryogenic facility to test full length SSC magnets under simulated operating conditions.
the design, construction and operation of a test stand capable of simulating SSC magnet operating conditions with a wide variety of refrigeration modes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this test stand is the first of its kind to be designed and built.
this is an excellent test stand for testing full length SSC magnets at temperatures from 2 K to 5 K.

this test stand has been designed to operate at the extreme of the cryogenic conditions of the SSC magnets, with the flexibility to accommodate the variety of operating conditions which are expected in the main ring, and with the reliability required of a facility for full-scale magnet testing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stand was designed and built in 1988 and has performed well in testing of SSC dipoles and quadrupoles.
the stand is fully functional, and we are currently performing tests on a 4.5 m dipole magnet with a 4.6 T central field.
this facility has been successfully used in testing of the Fermilab SSC dipole magnet, a 5 Tesla, 4 m length magnet.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the superfluid capability of the stand has been demonstrated.
the design and fabrication of a superfluid test stand can be accomplished with a modest budget and with the use of existing technology.
the test stand is fully operational, and the magnet under test is cooled and warmed with the cryogenics as designed.
